chapter_name: Chapter 20: Long Writing Skills Letters Paragraphs and Emails
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will construct structured paragraphs, understand the nuances between Formal and Informal letters, and master modern Email etiquette.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Ready to write longer pieces? Whether you're complaining to the mayor, updating a friend, or sending a quick professional email, you need the right structure to make your voice heard! Let's become master communicators! ✉️

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Formal letters (to principals, editors, businesses) follow a strict structure: Sender's Address, Date, Receiver's Address, Subject, Salutation, formal Body, and polite Sign-off (Yours faithfully/sincerely). Informal letters (to friends/family) skip the Receiver's Address and Subject, and use a warm, casual tone (Yours lovingly).
examples_or_templates: Formal Sign-off: Yours truly, / Yours sincerely,
Informal Salutation: Dearest Rahul, / Hi Mom,

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A good paragraph is like a burger! Top bun: The Topic Sentence (states the main idea). The Meat/Veggies: Supporting Sentences (give reasons, details, examples). Bottom bun: The Concluding Sentence (wraps up the idea). Use transition words (firstly, moreover, however) to connect your thoughts.
examples_or_templates: Topic Sentence: 'Reading habits deeply improve a student's vocabulary.'
Transition words: Furthermore, For instance, As a result, Consequently.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Emails are the modern letters. Key components: 'To' (receiver's ID), 'Cc' (Carbon Copy - to keep others informed), 'Bcc' (Blind Carbon Copy - hides the email ID from others). The 'Subject' line must be crisp and clear. Keep the body concise, use a professional greeting, and add an email signature.
examples_or_templates: Subject: Request for Leave - Amit Sharma (Class 8A)
Signature: Best regards, \n Amit Sharma \n Student Council Head

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ In an email, what does the abbreviation 'Bcc' stand for?
❓ Which of these is a required part of a Formal letter, but NOT an Informal letter?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write a clear and concise Subject line for a Formal Letter to the Editor complaining about frequent power cuts in your area.
subjective_practice.hint: Start with a phrase like 'Complaint regarding...'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write the 'Topic Sentence' for a paragraph about the importance of eating healthy food.
subjective_practice.hint: Make a strong opening statement that tells the reader exactly what the paragraph will be about.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Which sign-off is appropriate for an email to a teacher: 'Cheers', 'Yours lovingly', or 'Best regards'?
subjective_practice.hint: Teachers require a formal and respectful tone.

activity_or_assignment.title: 📩 Email to the Future You
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Draft a proper email addressed to yourself 5 years in the future! Fill in the To, Subject, Salutation, and Body (what are your goals? what do you hope to have achieved?). Use perfect email formatting!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Formal letters require strict formatting and a polite tone; Informal letters are casual and omit the receiver's address and subject.
⭐ A well-structured paragraph needs a Topic Sentence, Supporting Sentences, and a Concluding Sentence.
⭐ Emails require a clear subject line, professional greetings/sign-offs, and an understanding of To, Cc, and Bcc functions.
